answer: A harbor data exchange should not mistake a nebula of aliases for independent relays. During each round, independent auditors challenge all wharf relay identities simultaneously to transmit distinct, unpredictable byte streams before a deadline. Allocate service weight in proportion to authenticated bytes received, with no base weight per identity. Splitting one uplink among many aliases cannot multiply its measured capacity; more weight requires more bandwidth. Auditors must prevent replay and self-testing, and account for shared bottlenecks and colluding receivers.
